story.iWant: standardized error types and structured logging
story.soThat: errors are consistent and debuggable across all services
story.tasks:
- [ ] **T1 – Implement IdentiKey error type** - [ ] Create `src/lib/keycloak/errors.ts` exporting: - [ ] `class IdentiKeyError extends Error` with `message`, `code`, and optional `cause`. - [ ] A frozen `ErrorCodes` object enumerating at least: `USER_NOT_FOUND`, `APP_NOT_FOUND`, `GUILD_NOT_FOUND`, `AUTH_FLOW_NOT_FOUND`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, `CONNECTION_FAILED`, `INVALID_INPUT`. - [ ] Ensure stack traces are preserved and `name` is set to `"IdentiKeyError"`.
- [ ] **T2 – Implement shared logger** - [ ] Create `src/lib/keycloak/logger.ts` exporting a singleton `logger` from `pino`. - [ ] Configure `level` from `process.env.LOG_LEVEL ?? 'info'`. - [ ] In `NODE_ENV === 'development'`, enable `pino-pretty` transport for readable console output; otherwise emit plain JSON. - [ ] Add (or prepare for) redaction of obviously sensitive fields so they never appear in structured logs.
- [ ] **T3 – Wire into existing foundation** - [ ] Use `IdentiKeyError` as the canonical error type for connectivity/auth failures in `client.ts` (e.g. wrapping Keycloak admin client auth errors) without changing external APIs. - [ ] Use `logger` for connection validation and other core messages instead of `console.log` or ad-hoc logging.
- [ ] **T4 – Tests and safety checks** - [ ] Add unit tests verifying: - [ ] `IdentiKeyError` preserves message, code, and cause. - [ ] `ErrorCodes` is stable and treated as a closed set for current use cases. - [ ] `logger` honors `LOG_LEVEL` and does not throw during initialization. - [ ] Add at least one test or harness that exercises wrapping of a synthetic Keycloak/network error into `IdentiKeyError` with `CONNECTION_FAILED` or `UNAUTHORIZED`.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **IdentiKey error type and codes** - Given a Keycloak or network error occurs in a connectivity path (e.g. during configuration loading or Keycloak client initialization) When it is handled in the core layer Then it is wrapped in an `IdentiKeyError` instance with: - a specific, non-generic `code` drawn from a constrained `ErrorCodes` set, and - an optional `cause` preserving the original error for debugging.
2. **Structured logging with Pino** - Given the application is running in any environment When the logger is used from core modules (`config.ts`, `client.ts`, future services) Then logs are emitted via a shared `logger` built on `pino`, with: - JSON output by default in non-development environments, and - pretty-printed, human-readable output in development.
3. **Environment-driven log level** - Given `LOG_LEVEL` is set in the environment When the logger is created Then the effective log level honors `LOG_LEVEL`, defaulting to `info` when unset.
4. **No secret leakage** - Given errors are wrapped and logs are written When sensitive values such as passwords, tokens, client secrets, or full credential objects are involved Then those values are never logged (neither in messages nor in structured fields), and error messages remain high-level and non-leaky.
5. **Ready for Epic 1 consumers** - Given later epics introduce domain services (users, apps, guilds, roles, flows, sessions, events) When those services depend on the error and logging primitives from this story Then they can: - throw `IdentiKeyError` with appropriate codes without redesigning the base types, and - use the shared `logger` directly without additional per-service configuration.

doc.title: keycloak-commander — Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: - **NFR1:** Credentials (Keycloak admin password, client secrets) are never logged or exposed in error messages - **NFR2:** MCP server only accepts local connections (stdio transport, not network-exposed) - **NFR3:** CLI does not store credentials in command history (reads from env vars or prompts) - **NFR4:** All Keycloak API calls use HTTPS in production

doc.title: keycloak-commander — Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet:
As a **developer**, I want **standardized error types and structured logging**, So that **errors are consistent and debuggable across all services**.
Given a Keycloak API error occurs When it's caught in the service layer Then it's wrapped in `IdentiKeyError` with code, message, and cause
And pino logger is configured with:
- JSON output in production - Pretty output in development - Log level from `LOG_LEVEL` env var (default: `info`)
And sensitive data (passwords, secrets) is never logged

doc.title: Architecture — keycloak-commander
Epic Technical Specification: Epic 1 – Foundation
doc.snippet: Define standard error types (`IdentiKeyError`, error codes) and structured logging (`pino`) for all subsequent epics. Provide a connection validation mechanism that can be invoked at startup from CLI and MCP entrypoints, surfacing actionable diagnostics when Keycloak is unreachable or credentials are invalid. Once this epic is complete, higher-level epics can safely assume access to a typed, authenticated `KcAdminClient` instance, a validated configuration object, common logging and error primitives, and a `validateConnection()` routine that can be used by any entrypoint to gate startup.

artifact.reason: Loads and validates Keycloak connection and logging configuration from environment variables using Zod; error wrapping and logging behavior depend on this validated configuration.
Provides the singleton authenticated Keycloak admin client and connection validation hook where connectivity/auth failures will be wrapped into IdentiKeyError and logged via the shared logger.
Verifies configuration usage, singleton semantics, and connection validation behavior; will be extended to assert IdentiKeyError wrapping and logging semantics.
Defines the canonical IdentiKeyError type and constrained ErrorCodes set that all services will use for connectivity and domain failures.
Provides the shared Pino logger instance with environment-driven log level and dev-friendly pretty output, ensuring consistent structured logging across services.

story-context.constraints: - All connectivity and domain errors surfaced from the Keycloak boundary must be represented as `IdentiKeyError` instances with specific, non-generic codes from `ErrorCodes`. - Services and entrypoints must never log secrets, passwords, tokens, client secrets, or full credential objects; logs may only include high-level identifiers and scrubbed messages. - ErrorCodes is treated as a closed set for current use cases; introducing new codes requires updating the shared `ErrorCodes` constant rather than ad-hoc string literals. - Logging must be centralized through the shared `logger` instance from `logger.ts`; modules should avoid ad-hoc `console.log` usage. - Error handling and logging concerns live in the foundation layer (`errors.ts`, `logger.ts`, `client.ts`) so that higher-level services can be implemented without duplicating connectivity/error semantics.
story-context.interfaces:
- IdentiKeyError API: - `new IdentiKeyError(message: string, code: typeof ErrorCodes[keyof typeof ErrorCodes], cause?: Error)` - Extends Error, preserves stack traces, and sets `name` to `"IdentiKeyError"`.
- ErrorCodes: - A frozen object containing: - `USER_NOT_FOUND`, `APP_NOT_FOUND`, `GUILD_NOT_FOUND`, `AUTH_FLOW_NOT_FOUND`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, `CONNECTION_FAILED`, `INVALID_INPUT`.
- Logger API: - `logger` exported from `src/lib/keycloak/logger.ts` with standard Pino methods (`info`, `warn`, `error`, `debug`). - Configured with `level` from `LOG_LEVEL` (default `info`) and `pino-pretty` transport when `NODE_ENV === 'development'`.
- Client/Validation interplay: - `getKeycloakClient(): Promise<KcAdminClient>` — obtains a singleton authenticated client based on validated config. - `validateConnection(): Promise<void>` — uses the same client/auth path to perform a lightweight connectivity check and will surface failures wrapped in IdentiKeyError with appropriate codes.

tests.standards: Use Vitest for unit-level tests that focus on error-wrapping behavior and logger initialization; avoid real Keycloak I/O by mocking the admin client and environment. Prioritize tests that assert IdentiKeyError shape, ErrorCodes stability, and that logger initialization respects LOG_LEVEL and does not leak secrets into log payloads.
tests.ideas: - AC1: Simulate a Keycloak or network error during client authentication and verify it can be wrapped into an `IdentiKeyError` with an appropriate code (e.g. `CONNECTION_FAILED` or `UNAUTHORIZED`) and a preserved cause. - AC2: Verify that the shared logger respects `LOG_LEVEL`, emitting debug logs only when configured, and that JSON vs pretty output toggles with NODE_ENV without throwing during initialization. - AC3: Assert that obvious sensitive fields (passwords, tokens, client secrets) are never included in structured log objects, even when errors occur. - AC4: Confirm that services depending on the error and logging primitives can surface failures without needing to know about raw Keycloak error types. - AC5: Add a harness test around a synthetic connectivity/auth failure path that exercises both IdentiKeyError wrapping and logging, ensuring no secret leakage while still producing actionable diagnostics.
